instructions: Finely chop the onion. Grate the carrot. Dice the bell pepper and tomato small. Finely chop 1 inch of ginger and 2 tbsp of the cilantro. Toss it all together in a bowl with the salt.
Stir the batter. It should be thick enough to hold a shape when you spread it. Stir in a spoonful or two of water only if it won't spread at all.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium. Wipe it with a little of the oil.
Ladle about 1/2 cup batter into the skillet and spread it into a thick 5-inch round. Make a second one beside it.
Scatter about 1/4 cup of the vegetables over each round and press them in lightly. Drizzle a little oil around the edges.
Cover and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the bottom is golden and the top looks set. Flip and cook the other side, uncovered, for 2 minutes.
Transfer to a plate and repeat with the rest of the batter to make 6 in all.
Serve warm or at room temperature. For packed lunches, cool them fully and wrap them well. They keep in the fridge for 2 days, and reheat in a dry skillet over medium for 1 to 2 minutes per side.
method_notes: Hebbar's Kitchen leads (5 stars from 229) with the thick-batter, vegetable-on-top method and the onion, carrot, pepper, tomato, ginger and cilantro topping. Its batter is soaked, ground and fermented for about 13 hours, which isn't a lunch, so this uses ready-made idli dosa batter as Archana's Kitchen and Jeyashri's Kitchen do. Check the label: most are rice and urad dal only, so they're gluten-free and vegan. Curry leaves and the green chili from Hebbar's are left out to keep it mild.
